July 23, 2026

Iranian strike reported on US air base in Kuwait

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Reports indicate an Iranian strike hit Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait, with Iranian satellite imagery showing at least five barracks destroyed. The Pentagon has not confirmed the attack, and the imagery has not been contested; if the barracks were occupied, casualties are considered likely. Both Washington and Tehran are described as escalating rather than seeking an off-ramp, with Iran seeking to retain leverage over the Strait of Hormuz after the death of its supreme leader, while national average gasoline prices have reached $4.09 a gallon.

House passes war powers resolution as Republicans break with Trump on Iran

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas

The House of Representatives passed a war powers resolution aimed at curbing the president's ability to continue the war in Iran, with Republicans Fitzpatrick, Davidson, Massie and Barrett voting against the president. The vote is largely symbolic but has angered the White House because it signals that Republicans are not unified behind the war. Trump has argued such votes lead Iran to take a harder line in negotiations.

Houthi strikes on Saudi tankers close a second global trade chokepoint

tags: markets, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran-backed Houthi forces said they struck two Saudi oil tankers and began firing missiles and drones into the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which they described as enforcing a blockade on Saudi shipping in response to Saudi attacks on Yemen. The strait carries roughly 12% of global trade and had been Saudi Arabia's main route for bypassing the effectively closed Strait of Hormuz. Maritime insurers are declining coverage, pushing shipping around the Cape of Good Hope and adding 10 to 18 days per voyage, while Brent crude rose 4.8% to $98.59 a barrel and oil prices have since touched $100.

Massie says Pentagon is splitting the Iran war in two to evade war powers law

tags: politics, war, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Representative Thomas Massie said the Pentagon is presenting the conflict as two separate Iran wars divided by a brief cease-fire in order to avoid the 90-day limit on hostilities without congressional authorization, and accused the war secretary of breaking the law. The claim follows reporting that the Pentagon removed four service members who died in Jordan from its official casualty list, explaining that their deaths occurred after the president declared a cease-fire in April.

Trump tells communities they cannot fight data centers as local opposition grows

tags: tech, politics, climate
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos

Speaking to governors, Trump said communities cannot fight data centers and must embrace them, arguing the projects bring jobs, local revenue that can offset property taxes, and investment in job training, and claiming foreign countries are funding public relations campaigns against them. He also said some communities are eager for the facilities while opponents are motivated by wanting projects to go elsewhere. Communities across the country are organizing against data centers over air pollution and water use, including a proposed Utah facility larger than Manhattan.

SpaceX and Blue Origin push plan for more than a million orbital data centers

tags: tech, climate
sources: @aaronparnas

SpaceX and Blue Origin are advancing plans to place over a million data centers in orbit. Experts cited in a petition filed by Earthjustice warn the scheme would generate significant pollution from satellites and rockets burning up on re-entry, releasing soot, rare metals, aluminum oxides and other compounds with unknown effects. Some scientists say the resulting pollution could destroy the ozone layer and return to Earth.

Utah data center next to Great Salt Lake draws bipartisan backlash

tags: climate, politics, tech
sources: @carolinegleich

A data center proposed by Kevin O'Leary in Box Elder County, Utah, next to the Great Salt Lake has drawn sustained public opposition that has already forced a reduction in the project's size and contributed to some Republicans losing office. Critics say the project was advanced through a quasi-governmental agency without any public comment period or environmental review. Opponents describe the coalition as including Republicans, ranchers and farmers across the state.

ICE to resume vehicle stops nationwide under new internal limits

tags: immigration, surveillance
sources: @oafnation_actual

DHS whistleblowers say an internal ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations memo will allow vehicle stops to resume nationwide when deemed operationally necessary. Under the policy, stops may only be conducted by officers who have completed federal vehicle stop training, and at least one officer on scene must have an issued and activated body-worn camera. Stops are also permitted when tied to a criminal arrest or search warrant with an ICE special response team officer present.

Epstein survivor's family urges senators to reject Todd Blanche as attorney general

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Amanda and Sky Roberts, family of Epstein survivor Virginia Roberts Giuffre, released an open letter urging two Republican senators to vote against Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general and to meet with survivors. The letter calls the vote a defining moment for truth and accountability. The White House is working to secure the senators' support, and the nomination is reported to lack the votes at present.

Claims that Epstein evidence was suppressed before investigations began

tags: legal, politics
sources: @cancel.ian.carroll

It was argued that existing Epstein files contain enough evidence to open numerous investigations and hold dozens of perpetrators accountable. The account states the original investigation was obstructed internally, that the New Mexico ranch was never raided and the island was not searched until August 2019 after Epstein's death, and that investigators photographed binders of discs and hard drives at his New York townhouse without seizing them because they fell outside the warrant's scope. When agents returned with a new warrant days later the material was gone, and only some of it later surfaced through Epstein's own attorney.

CDC website edited to question vaccine-autism evidence

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A page on the official CDC website was quietly changed to state that the claim vaccines do not cause autism is not evidence-based because studies have not ruled out the possibility. The change contradicts peer-reviewed research. Concerns were raised that because the text sits on a government site, AI systems and students researching the question will reproduce it as authoritative.

SAVE Act attached to Iran emergency funding bill through budget loophole

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Republicans have folded a version of the SAVE Act into a roughly $95 billion emergency funding package tied to the war in Iran and domestic support including agriculture, allotting $10 billion for election infrastructure such as ID-checking systems. Because the provision carries a budget appropriation, it could qualify for passage in the Senate with 51 votes rather than a filibuster-proof majority, though the parliamentarian will have to rule on what is permissible. Attaching it to funding for troops abroad adds political pressure on members of both parties.

Education Department rule would cut student loans from low-earning degree programs

tags: politics, education
sources: @aaronparnas

The Department of Education is advancing a new accountability test under which undergraduate programs whose graduates do not out-earn workers who never attended college could lose access to federal student loans. Officials frame it as ending federal underwriting of degrees that do not raise earnings. Critics say the standard could disqualify many liberal arts programs and, in states such as Florida, affect loans for teaching degrees. The rule could take effect as early as next year.

McConnell's hospitalization passes 39 days amid Kentucky ballot deadline scrutiny

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

Senator Mitch McConnell is reported to remain a patient at George Washington University Hospital more than 39 days after arriving by ambulance, with no public information about his condition and vehicles resembling a security detail outside. Access to the building is restricted and staff have declined to comment. Attention has turned to Kentucky's election calendar, where August 11, 2026 is the final deadline for candidates to file for a vacancy occurring after the June deadline, prompting claims that any announcement about his status will come only after that date.

Trump presses Senate Republicans to end the filibuster

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump said he would sit at home and cry if Senate Republicans do not terminate the filibuster and pass his Save America Act agenda, arguing that Democrats would otherwise do so and gain 40 electoral votes by making the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico states. There is not currently enough support among Senate Republicans to eliminate the filibuster.

Trump ties proposed US-Saudi nuclear deal to Abraham Accords membership

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump said a proposed nuclear agreement between the United States and Saudi Arabia depends on Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords. Any deal would still require congressional approval.

Five Palestinians killed in Gaza strike and West Bank violence

tags: war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Officials said five Palestinians were killed Thursday in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza and in separate violence in the occupied West Bank.

Greece approves $4 billion Israeli air-defense system

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Greece approved the purchase of a $4 billion Israeli air-defense system as part of a broader military modernization plan.

Americans outside the labor force hit a record 105.8 million

tags: markets, economy
sources: @oafnation_actual

The number of Americans not participating in the labor force climbed to a record 105.8 million in June, exceeding the peak reached during the COVID-19 pandemic. Traders are pricing in a 12% probability that the US unemployment rate rises to 5% at some point in 2026.

Veterinarians urge Congress to reject Save Our Bacon Act in farm bill

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Republicans in Congress are advancing the Save Our Bacon Act, which would invalidate state animal welfare laws requiring that farm animals have room to turn around, lie down and extend their limbs. The provision is pending in the farm bill, which senators are currently marking up ahead of consideration in the coming weeks before the midterm elections. Hundreds of veterinarians have joined calls for Congress to reject it.

West Virginia Republican delegate charged with attempting to entice a minor

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Elliot Pritt, a West Virginia Republican delegate who had pledged to protect children from the LGBTQIA and drag community, has been arrested and charged with attempting to entice a 15-year-old minor on Roblox and Snapchat.

Andrew Tate says he is being held in solitary confinement

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Andrew Tate said he is being held in a special housing unit under the highest level of security, without commissary, visits or contact with the outside world, and described a neighboring inmate screaming through the night. He is facing extradition on serious criminal charges. The complaint was posted to his social media account, which he could not access directly from custody.
